key_insight: A differentiable JAX shell solver enables GPU-accelerated, large-deformation aortic-valve simulations with contact using matrix-free tangent evaluations.
engineering_relevance: Faster patient-specific valve simulations could support studies of how tissue properties and geometry affect leaflet deformation and coaptation.
method: Energy-based finite elements combine extensible-director shells, hyperelasticity, and finite-range repulsive contact.
Regularized Newton–Krylov equilibrium solves use two-level preconditioning.
Automatic differentiation computes tangent-vector products, while GPUs parallelize element and quadrature calculations.
evidence_signal: Component benchmarks and contact-free sensitivity checks supported verification; three patient-specific valves reached relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4, with median GPU runtimes of approximately 15–25 minutes and 5.3–6.5× CPU speedups on tested hardware.
watch_item: Sensitivity validation was limited to a contact-free plate; gradient-based inverse studies with evolving valve contact remain future work.
paper_title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
